verbatim_quote: Foreign intermediary electronic marketplaces will be considered responsible for the VAT of the non-resident. This marketplace liability was introduced in April 2019.
notes: Marketplace deemed supplier rules introduced April 2019 under section 54(2B) of the VAT Act. Amended effective 1 April 2025: intermediaries may now act on behalf of principals irrespective of the principal's VAT registration status, provided both parties agree in writing (RSM / EY sources). Principal and intermediary are jointly and severally liable for VAT on deemed supplies. Registration threshold is ZAR 1,000,000 in any consecutive 12-month period. Standard VAT rate was 15% at time of marketplace rule enactment; scheduled increases to 15.5% on 1 May 2025 and 16% on 1 April 2026 per globalvatcompliance.com. B2C low-value import VAT (removing de minimis exemption below ZAR 500) came into effect 1 September 2024. B2B exclusion from 'electronic services' definition effective 1 April 2025 means foreign suppliers serving only SA VAT-registered vendors need not register. USD equivalent of ZAR 1,000,000 registration threshold not explicitly stated in sources; left as null.
